title: Cell cycle and HIF-1 related gene expression alteration in thyroid cell lines under microgravity.
one_liner_zh: 该研究分析模拟微重力下甲状腺细胞系的基因表达变化及迁移侵袭能力，属于纯转录组和细胞表型实验，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: With growing interest in space exploration, understanding microgravity's impact on human health is essential. This study aims to investigate gene expression changes and migration and invasion potential in five thyroid-related cell lines cultured under simulated microgravity. METHODS: Five thyroid-related cell lines-normal thyrocytes (Nthy-ori 3-1), papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) cells (SNU-790, TPC-1), poorly differentiated thyroid cancer cell (BCPAP), and anaplastic thyroid cancer cell (SNU-80)-were cultured under simulated microgravity (10(-3) g) using a clinostat. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were analyzed using cDNA microarray, followed by functional annotation and assessment of aggressiveness via Transwell migration and invasion assays. RESULTS: DEG analysis under simulated microgravity revealed distinct gene expression profiles by gravity condition, with 2980 DEGs in SNU-790, 1033 in BCPAP, 562 in TPC-1, 477 in Nthy-ori 3-1, and 246 in SNU-80, as confirmed by hierarchical clustering. In PTC cell lines (SNU-790, TPC-1), G2-M phase-related genes were upregulated. In non-PTC cell lines (BCPAP, SNU-80), genes associated with innate immune response, Toll-like receptor signaling, were upregulated, whereas Hypoxia-Inducible Factor 1-alpha (HIF-1alpha) signaling-related genes were downregulated. Additionally, under simulated microgravity, significant migration was observed in SNU-790 (3 x 10(4) cells) and BCPAP (2 x 10(4) and 3 x 10(4)), while significant invasion occurred in SNU-790, Nthy-ori 3-1, and BCPAP at a seeding density of 2 x 10(4). Other conditions showed no significant differences. CONCLUSION: This study comprehensively evaluates the effects of simulated microgravity using a diverse panel of thyroid-related cell lines. These findings provide valuable insight into how microgravity could influence cancer biology, emphasizing the importance of further research on cancer behavior in space environments and its implications for human health during long-term space missions.
abstract_zh: 背景：随着人类对太空探索兴趣的日益增长，理解微重力对健康的影响至关重要。本研究旨在探讨在模拟微重力条件下培养的五种甲状腺相关细胞系中的基因表达变化及迁移和侵袭能力。方法：使用回转器（clinostat）在模拟微重力（10(-3) g）条件下培养五种甲状腺相关细胞系——正常甲状腺细胞（Nthy-ori 3-1）、乳头状甲状腺癌（PTC）细胞（SNU-790、TPC-1）、低分化甲状腺癌细胞（BCPAP）以及未分化甲状腺癌细胞（SNU-80）。通过cDNA微阵列分析差异表达基因（DEGs），随后进行功能注释，并利用Transwell迁移和侵袭实验评估细胞侵袭性。结果：在模拟微重力下的DEG分析揭示了不同重力条件下的独特基因表达谱，其中SNU-790中有2980个DEGs，BCPAP中有1033个，TPC-1中有562个，Nthy-ori 3-1中有477个，SNU-80中有246个，并通过层次聚类得到确认。在PTC细胞系（SNU-790、TPC-1）中，G2-M期相关基因表达上调。在非PTC细胞系（BCPAP、SNU-80）中，与先天免疫应答、Toll样受体信号传导相关的基因表达上调，而缺氧诱导因子1-α（HIF-1alpha）信号传导相关基因表达下调。此外，在模拟微重力下，SNU-790（3 x 10(4) 细胞）和BCPAP（2 x 10(4) 和 3 x 10(4)）观察到显著迁移，而SNU-790、Nthy-ori 3-1和BCPAP在接种密度为2 x 10(4)时发生显著侵袭。其他条件下未见显著差异。结论：本研究利用多种甲状腺相关细胞系全面评估了模拟微重力的影响。这些发现为微重力如何影响癌症生物学提供了宝贵见解，强调了在太空环境中进一步研究癌症行为及其对长期太空任务中人类健康影响的重要性。
